items.prompt: Black has castled queenside and White kingside, so the kings are on opposite wings. Black to move. Find the pawn lever: a pawn move that attacks a pawn in front of the enemy king.

claims.statement: The white king stands on g1.
The black king stands on c8, so the kings are on opposite wings.
The pawn moves after which the moved pawn attacks the White pawn on h3 are exactly g4.
g4 is the engine's best move, and every accepted move is within 30 centipawns of it (depth 16).
The quieter Bb6 is at least 4 pawns worse than g4 (depth 16).

hints: A lever is a pawn move that attacks one of the pawns shielding the enemy king.
Look for a pawn that can step forward next to the White pawn on h3.
The pawn move ends on a square that attacks h3.
items.explain: g4 is a lever: it attacks the pawn on h3. At depth 16 the engine rates it at least 4 pawns above Bb6. This is an engine result for this one position, not a rule that pawn storms win.

items.prompt: White to move. Your rook can take on f2, and the rook trade looks natural. Before you trade, ask which of your pieces the trade would remove from the defence. Find a better move.

Qc4+ is among the engine's best moves, within 30 centipawns of the best (depth 16).
The trade Rxf2 is at least three pawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Ask what the rook that would trade is currently guarding, and who guards it afterwards.
Check your back rank: after the trade, can the enemy pieces give check there?
The trade Rxf2 is not the best idea here. Look for a move that keeps your pieces working together.
items.explain: The only black piece guarding f2 is the queen on f6, but after Rxf2 Qxf2+ the white rook that held the back rank is gone and the engine finds a forced mate. At depth 16 the engine rates Rxf2 at least three pawns below the best move. A trade can take away your own defender as well as the enemy attacker. This is one position checked by an engine, not a rule that rook trades lose.
